claims.text: Post-processing annealing at approximately 700–800°C improves the tensile ductility of HfZrTiTa0.53 relative to the untreated condition.
The annealing treatment improves tensile uniform elongation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The annealing treatment preserves the alloy's high compressive strength.
The annealing treatment preserves impact-triggered energy release.
HfZrTiTa0.53 is fabricated by high-temperature consolidation.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal compressive strain of approximately 13.5%.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility.
Intermediate-temperature annealing relieves residual stresses in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Intermediate-temperature annealing reconfigures grain boundaries and produces a favorable grain-size distribution.
The annealing-induced microstructure enhances activation of multiple slip systems during tensile loading.
Controlled annealing enables microstructural recovery without excessive grain growth or significant phase coarsening.
Residual-stress relief and controlled microstructural recovery improve uniform plastic deformation under tension.
Annealing increases room-temperature, quasi-static tensile uniform elongation by approximately 10–20% relative to the untreated baseline.
Annealing reduces yield strength by less than 5% relative to the untreated baseline.
Annealing reduces compressive strength by less than 5% relative to the untreated baseline.
The impact energy release of annealed HfZrTiTa0.53 remains comparable to that of the unannealed alloy.
As-processed HfZrTiTa0.53 has established impact-triggered energy-release properties.
Excessively high annealing temperatures or prolonged durations cause undesirable grain growth that compromises strength and impact performance.
